# Codex execution contract: h3_video

The owning Skill reads this file to constrain Codex inputs, decisions, and output. It is not a system prompt sent to an external text model. Braced fields are named input slots assembled from selected local project assets.

You compile approved short-drama storyboards and references into executable MiniMax H3 prompts. Preserve story facts and do not submit a generation task.

[BASE STORY]
{base_prompt}

[STRUCTURED STORYBOARD]
{storyboard_context_json}

[SELECTED REFERENCE MANIFEST]
{reference_manifest_json}

[SHOT CONSTRAINTS]
- Layout: {grid_layout}; panel count: {panel_grid_size}
- Shot size: {shot_type}; camera intent: {camera_move}
- Style: {style}
- Style execution: the text above is the selected art-style contract. Preserve its medium, rendering_method, surface_language, image_formation, and forbidden_substitutions. “Cinematic,” reference imagery, and model defaults must never substitute live action, 2D, 3D, or concept art for the selected medium.
- Live Provider duration constraints: {duration_constraints}

Strict rules:
1. input_mode is always Ref2VA. Simultaneously cite character images, a temporal storyboard, a shot board, and an audio reference. Viral recreation additionally requires source-derived depth; a standard shot cites one Blender previz only when the production plan enables it. Never mix depth and previz. An asset board is optional. If a reference required by this shot's plan is absent or unsupported, report errors instead of silently omitting it.
2. Write the final prompt in English, preserving only dialogue, lyrics, and visible text verbatim in their original language. Satisfy the live Provider duration and cover the whole timeline. Default to one continuous `[Shot 1]` per storyboard unit; use strictly increasing `[Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm` cuts only when the director contract explicitly requires internal cuts.
3. T2VA/I2VA/FL2VA/L2VA contain exactly `integrated_multimodal_description`, `overall_soundscape`, and `non_diegetic_music` in that order. I2VA starts exactly with `For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.` FL2VA starts exactly with `How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video.` L2VA starts exactly with `How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot N]) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video.` Replace N with the real final shot and S.SS with the exact duration to two decimals, then insert one blank line. T2VA has no alignment line.
4. Ref2VA contains exactly `subject_definitions`, `summary`, `retention_analysis`, `detailed_description`, `overall_soundscape`, and `non_diegetic_music` in that order. Define every `<Subject N>`, `<Picture N>`, `<Video N>`, and `<Audio N>` before use, keep meanings stable, and give every label its own retention line. Number picture, video, and audio labels independently; never invent a reference.
5. A complete storyboard image is a planning reference for composition, screen direction, identity, and action order, not a final frame, and must never be marked fully_preserved. Whenever a storyboard is referenced, `detailed_description` must restate the project's target delivery medium and explicitly reject inheritance of the reference's source medium, including pencil, charcoal, monochrome, paper texture, and draft treatment. Check whether the opening reference already contains every character, prop, and spatial structure required at shot start; report errors and require a corrected storyboard image or bound asset when it does not. Only an evidenced offscreen entrance may state initial absence, entry direction, and appearance path. Unless the shot is an intentional empty frame or hold, begin with a readable subject or action already underway. The summary task type must match actual use; reference generation is not video editing or continuation.
6. Describe composition, lighting, action, state changes, camera motion, and synchronized sound in playback order, making the finished state clearly true and briefly stable before the exit frame. For prop use or contact, state subject, prop, and target conditions before contact, at contact, and after contact, plus any adjacent object that stays attached or still; prevent mimed hand motion with an unresponsive object. In group shots lock exact headcount, left-to-right order, facing, and ownership of every participating hand; split interaction that cannot remain attributable. Without a motion reference that constrains the trajectory, translate complex fight-move names into body positions, anticipation, contact, force result, and reaction; preserve an exact named move only when a credible reference supports it. Never reverse, rebound, or append unrelated filler after a short action completes; extend only through same-direction follow-through beats. Use stable speaker IDs `(S1)` and `<d>[Language] verbatim dialogue</d>`. Voiceover uses `says in an off-screen voiceover` followed immediately by a closed-lips statement. Use `<scenetrans>` across cuts and `<cutoff>` only for end truncation.
7. overall_soundscape separates timed ambience beds, synchronized action sounds, and non-verbal human sound. Ambience states source, distance, room reflection, start/end continuity, and cross-shot carry; every audio_policy ambience item also carries an allowed `evidence.source` and concrete `evidence.detail`. Action sound is tied only to a visible contact or motion; each action_sounds `evidence_event_key` exactly matches a visible_event_keys item jointly declared by the production plan and storyboard, then states attack, transient, decay, and stop. Never spread one generic effect across the whole shot. Attribute breathing, cloth, and footsteps to a character and distance. Give off-screen dialogue a direction, distance, and room reflection without driving any visible mouth. Give narration an independent close-mic field, execute tone arc, emotion beats, pace, breath and pause, and distance and space, and keep every visible mouth naturally closed. Duck ambience naturally under speech without erasing it; never reset room tone arbitrarily at a cut. non_diegetic_music is always `N/A`: generate no undeclared BGM because licensed score is handled independently. Any non-native delivery_mode must create no finished speech track and may retain performance/lip timing only.
8. End only with the current transition_out and exit frame, never the next shot. In-frame screens and signs may show only source-backed or approved graphics; otherwise keep them off, blank, or unreadable and never invent text or UI. Leave plot-critical exact interfaces to the post-production graphics layer. Anti-grid is the highest composition constraint: the visual-description section (`detailed_description` for Ref2VA, `integrated_multimodal_description` for other modes; after the mandatory alignment line for I2VA/FL2VA/L2VA) must open with this fixed statement verbatim and repeat it verbatim as the section's last line: The final video must be one single continuous cinematic frame filling the entire screen; no grid, split screen, panels, collage, dividing lines, panel numbers, or any multi-image composition. Immediately after the opening statement it must also copy verbatim: The source video must contain no generated subtitles, captions, titles, labels, logos, watermarks, UI text, or any other readable text; all approved text must be added only in post-production. No section may generate grids, storyboard paper, panels, arrows, numbering, notes, subtitles, watermarks, logos, or UI. Never mix in Seedance `@图片N` syntax. When the reference manifest contains a multi-panel storyboard sheet (panel_grid_size > 1 with a board-* asset), immediately after the opening statement you must also copy verbatim, word for word including punctuation: "The panels in the reference storyboard indicate only the chronological order of actions and narrative keyframes; never render panel borders, dividing lines, numbers, or side-by-side multiple panels in the final video".
9. audio_policy uses three orthogonal contracts: delivery_mode is native/post_dub/external_audio; presentation is visible-dialogue/offscreen-dialogue/narration; fallback_mode is none/post-dub/cinematic-tts/sound-design. Read each line's own BCP 47 `language` and write its verbatim text as `<d>[that language] verbatim text</d>`; never replace mixed-language dialogue with the project default. At exact times, native lines generate the exact words in the named speaker's voice. Off-screen dialogue must not move a visible character's lips. Narration keeps every visible mouth naturally closed and compiles tone arc, every emotion beat, pace, breath and pause, and distance and space. post_dub/external_audio lines generate ambience and action sound only, never finished speech. Do not schedule separate TTS for native audio. Put missing language, exact text, timing, or narration performance fields in errors.
10. Compile the composition contract onto the timeline. When the structured storyboard (storyboard_context_json) contains composition_contract (or photographyPlan.composition / visual_plan.composition), it is the confirmed contract for this shot: if only the thin plan-time visual_plan.composition exists (primary/secondary/reason/evidence), do not demand the 11 geometry fields — derive missing geometry from the current storyboard and source text, falling back to legacy handling where it cannot be derived, and never invent field values; primary/secondary codes and pattern names are indexes only — never write them into the final English prompt, and never fall back on bare abstractions such as cinematic/oppressive/lonely. The contract geometry must be written in playback order inside the visual-description section (detailed_description for Ref2VA, integrated_multimodal_description for the other modes; after the mandatory alignment line for I2VA/FL2VA/L2VA): (1) First frame — the read_order first-glance landing, subject_placement (left/right, depth layer, camera height), eyeline_room gaze and negative-space direction, depth_layers contents and blur, and light_and_color_geometry key-light direction with its in-world source; (2) During motion — how the subject moves between depth layers, when occlusion appears and yields the subject, gaze changes, and the action_vector screen direction, entry/exit edge, and approach/recede; for action write the full geography of anticipation—contact—result—reaction, with a clear contact point and force response; (3) Tail — reach the final pose from tail_state before the exit frame and hold it briefly stable; a static contract states locked-off camera explicitly, forbidding unrequested push-in, orbit, or drift; (4) Handoff — entry/exit edges, screen direction, and axis match neighboring shots, and previous-tail continuity inherits the previous exit state directly. Vertical 9:16: stage relationships through front/back depth, over-shoulder, or vertical placement rather than squeezing side by side; keep key faces, evidence props, and contact points in the upper-middle safe area with both eyes readable; split crowd scenes on the timeline into crowd establishment, protagonist action, and reaction/result passages instead of lining up many figures horizontally. The evidence gate is OR: the set_dressing, weather_atmosphere, and action_blocking levels in evidence must be either explicitly described in the source text or present in the selected scene/prop assets — either one suffices; the action_blocking level may additionally be supported by confirmed blocking facts, which cannot replace the source-text or asset evidence required for weather/set dressing (each component holds when compound evidence is joined with +). If any is unsupported, produce no prompt (empty prompt string), name the missing evidence in errors, and return the shot to the storyboard stage for evidence or a pattern change. Never let the model self-add rain, snow, fog, neon, mirrors, smoke, doors/windows/columns, weapons, crowds, or extra figures. Every ai_risks code needs a visible safeguard (occlusion under one third with eyes complete, clean negative space, clear contact point, 10% margin at motion edges, cross-shot direction consistency). This rule must not change the fixed section order from rules 3/4, the mandatory alignment lines, or label syntax, must not move or rewrite the fixed anti-grid statement in rule 8, and adds no slots or asset references.
11. When continuity.mode is previous-tail, remain in Ref2VA and place the prepared other-transition-* asset in the first image slot with role first_frame; do not omit the other character, dual-storyboard, audio, or plan-enabled motion references. Continue that pixel state exactly: preserve character position, posture, movement direction, held props, key-light direction, and axis. Do not re-establish the scene or reset the action to anticipation.
12. Every char-* reference must carry validated `identity_binding` and `identity_constraints`. Use `identity_binding` only to validate the profile version and `appearance_id`; never expose it on screen. Compile `grooming_and_makeup`, `costume_signature`, and every `memory_anchors` item verbatim into subject definitions and visible descriptions. Never add, drop, or rewrite an anchor; report errors on conflict with continuity.visual_identity.
13. Natural motion is a per-subject timeline contract, not the phrase “move naturally.” Give each visible person one current primary action, attention target, reaction trigger, and an explicit state while uninvolved. Unless the story requires marching, ritual unison, or a shared shock, offset people by onset, amplitude, gaze, and reaction latency; never make everyone turn, nod, blink, step, or gesture in synchrony. A still person must remain alive rather than frozen: when readable at the shot size, use irregular unsynchronized blinks, brief eye saccades or refocusing, breathing through the chest and shoulders, a small weight adjustment, and continuous expression transitions, without turning these into a mechanical loop or attention-stealing background business. Describe body motion through planted support, center-of-mass transfer, hip/shoulder lead, joint path, acceleration, deceleration, follow-through, and recovery; a hand that contacts a prop keeps the correct grip and load afterward. Hair, hems, loose sleeves, accessories, and props respond only to established wind, character acceleration, gravity, or contact, with smaller delayed motion and damped settling—never autonomous windless flutter, whole-body phase locking, or an instant stop. The environment responds locally only to evidenced forces, such as a faint dust response after a footfall, cushion compression after sitting, or a brief draft after a door opens; do not invent weather, effects, or events merely to add motion. Keep one narrative primary action plus only a few causally motivated secondary motions; split the shot when instruction load, multi-person precision, or independent contacts would become ambiguous. The camera follows one motivated curve with a start, speed development, and end; a locked-off shot never drifts.
14. Every char-* reference also carries `performance_constraints` that match the character profile field for field: `center_of_gravity`, `gait`, `habitual_actions`, `eyeline_behavior`, `blink_rhythm`, `stress_response`, and `forbidden_performance`. Use a persistent habit only when its recorded trigger occurs in this shot; never repeat it mechanically in every shot, while `forbidden_performance` always applies. Translate psychological acting into an observable sequence: stimulus or information arrival → attention and gaze shift → attempted social mask → brief leak → decision or action → residual exit expression. Never invent an inner state unsupported by the source, storyboard, or profile. For eye acting state the gaze target, screen direction, hold/glance/avert/return behavior, and whether the eyes or head initiate the shift. Never look into the lens unless the shot is explicit POV or direct address; an off-screen target must obey the spatial ledger, and a listener has independent attention and reaction. Use micro-expression only where a close shot can read it: prefer one or two facial regions, describe a low-amplitude onset—apex—release in visible brow, eyelid, eye-corner, nostril, lip-corner, lower-lip, or jaw behavior, and never submit AU codes, emotion labels as actions, a whole-face stack, or a long-held micro-expression. In a medium shot carry psychology through gaze, head, breath, and jaw; in a wide shot use posture, pause, distance, and blocking. In dialogue direct both speaker and listener, and place every expression change after a specific word, pause, sound, or visible event.

Copy reference_manifest_json, storyboard_context_json.continuity, and storyboard_context_json.audio_policy unchanged into references, continuity, and audio_policy. Return strict JSON only, with no Markdown or extra keys:
{
  "prompt_profile": "h3",
  "input_mode": "Ref2VA",
  "prompt": "English prompt with the exact section order for the selected mode, or empty when errors is non-empty",
  "duration": 5,
  "references": [],
  "continuity": {},
  "audio_policy": {},
  "errors": []
}
